speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Time saved from automating such services can be redirected to frontline core policing duties where human touch is crucial.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Another key aspect of policing is community partnership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In 2018, SPF introduced a new vocation for its voluntary service vocation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I attended the training graduation of the inaugural batch of 38 VSC (Community) officers in April 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: From 38 officers, we now have 134 VSC (Community) officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Dressed in a blue Police polo T-shirt and black cargo pants, VSC (Community) officers join regular Police Officers at high visibility patrols in community areas, assist in crowd and traffic regulation, and security checks at major security events.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: VSC (Community) is an example of how the community can help augment Police resources and contribute to our nation’s security.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked how we are reskilling our officers to better utilise technology and whether there is scope to form training committees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Home Team recognises the importance of upskilling our officers to take on higher value work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is crucial as we transform, introduce new concepts of operations, and redesign existing jobs to leverage new technologies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MHA formed a Skills Transformation Development Team to identify the training required for officers to meet increasing operational expectations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The team identified a need to develop officers' skills in key areas, such as data analytics, technology literacy and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Desmond Choo also asked about the re-employment of officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We aim to re-employ as many of our officers as we can.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I will now turn to my third area – keeping Singapore drug-free.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, this is a top priority for MHA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about Singapore’s views on the moves by some countries to legalise the use of cannabis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Government’s stand on illicit drugs, including cannabis, is clear.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Research has shown that they lead to irreversible brain damage, and even death.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Contrary to evidence, they portray raw cannabis as "harmless" and even having "health benefits".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The trend is largely driven by commercial lobbying thirsty for profits and serves as a politically expedient way out of a drug abuse situation over which some governments have lost control.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Public interest and the welfare of individuals, families and societies are sacrificed on the altars of bad science, profits and political expediency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Preventive education is our first line of defence against the drug scourge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked about MHA's plans to engage youths on the harms of drug abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Today, CNB reaches out to students through talks, roadshows, social media and projects.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: With their talents and passion, youths can be powerful anti-drug advocates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Nanyang Polytechnic graduates Jillian Khoo and Teh Yu Yin produced an illustrated book titled "Captain Drug Buster vs Dr Wacko: The Final Showdown".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The storybook teaches our 7- to 10-year-olds on the harms of drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Teachers and parents can read to their children and equip them with the facts about the harms of drugs early.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: You can get this storybook at primary school, public and Parliament libraries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Another example: 19-year-old Singaporean, Ms Nur Afikah, participated in the annual UN Office on Drugs and Crime Youth Forum in March 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: At the Forum, she exchanged ideas with representatives from 25 other countries on running effective programmes to prevent drug abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: She spoke from personal experience, having witnessed the devastating impact of drugs on relatives and friends.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: At the 2019 Youth Forum, Singapore will be represented by Javier Ng, a 17-year-old Institute of Technical Education (ITE) student.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Javier and Afikah are among 122 youth Anti-Drug Abuse Advocates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our youth advocates have organised various events, most recently, an anti-drug roadshow at the Singapore Institute of Management.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Acts of contamination which facilitate or promote drug use have been criminalised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Drug abusers who leave drugs lying around at home and expose children to the risks of drugs, will also be criminally liable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will also strengthen our drug rehabilitation regime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will make a distinction between abusers who only consume drugs, and those who face charges for other offences of harm to society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A key factor that keeps offenders from re-offending is strong pro-social support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Prisons have set up the Family Interventions and Reintegration Support Team in July 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Under this trial, Family Case Managers work closely with community partners to strengthen dysfunctional families, so that they can support and be meaningfully involved in the rehabilitation of their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: With strong family support, the reintegration process for the inmate becomes easier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As mentioned by Mr Saktiandi Supaat, unfortunately, there are still cases where ex-offenders are unable to return home due to unresolved family grievances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For help, they can go to the Singapore Anti-Narcotics Association's Step-Up Centre in Sengkang and the newly opened centre in Taman Jurong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They may also call the ComCare hotline or approach the nearest Social Service Office or Family Service Centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: If they have no alternative family support and are unable to afford other housing options, they can apply to the Housing and Development Board for public rental housing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There are schemes to support those in need, and inmates are briefed on help avenues before release.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are constantly reviewing to see how else we can support ex-offenders in their reintegration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: It is a difficult journey, but ex-offenders must also take ownership and responsibility for their reintegration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The community is another critical component of pro-social support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Malay-Muslim community has made significant efforts to mobilise support against drugs and for ex-offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I will speak in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: But this issue has been haunting our Malay community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Malay drug abusers form the biggest proportion of abusers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: It is worrying that the proportion of new Malay drug abusers and those aged below 30 are increasing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our community, however, is not easily defeated, and will not give up easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The war against the drug menace will continue to be fought with the strong support of the Government, Malay/Muslim organisations, religious leaders, families and our Malay youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam mentioned the Dadah Itu Haram Campaign that was launched in April 2017.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Dadah Itu Haram campaign harnesses the community's strength and demonstrates the community's firm stance against the scourge of drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Although only two years old, the Dadah Itu Haram campaign is not moving at a slow pace but, in fact, has reached out to the community very quickly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Every fortnight, our volunteers distribute Dadah Itu Haram campaign collaterals at mosques across Singapore after Friday prayers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Barbers share about the dangers of drugs at their barbershops while cutting hair.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As the Singapore Sepaktakraw Federation (PERSES) sepaktakraw league play their sepaktakraw, they actively help to spread anti-drug messages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Food stalls, music jamming studios, as well as car dealers and workshops also participate by sticking Dadah Itu Haram campaign decals as a reminder and a call for vigilance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to alert our community about the threat of drugs and take action so that our families and our children are conscious of the dangers and are protected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I am proud that we now receive interest from members of our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They want to contribute to the success of this campaign.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They feel like it is a calling to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Examples are our fishing brothers from The One Nation Angler Association (TONA); the cycling group Flow Riders; and the National University of Singapore Malay Society with their annual Paradigma event which reaches out to help youth abusers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Dadah Itu Haram campaign is a Community Campaign, the Voice from People’s Heart.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Apart from the Dadah Itu Haram campaign, organisations, such as Jamiyah, Pertapis, the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS) and the Muslim Counselling Service, provide support to ex-abusers while they are in and out of prison.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I salute AMP for its determination and sincerity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: AMP is the first organisation to provide all-round continuous support, from in-care counselling, family support, to support after their release.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Second, the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MUIS has produced sermons which are delivered during Friday prayers for inmates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This special sermon focuses on the needs of drug abusers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Additionally, religious teachers in MUIS are developing a religious education curriculum that will equip inmates in not only religious knowledge, but also values, such as responsibility to self and family, self-confidence and the importance of staying away from drugs that destroy families and degrades morals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MUIS and the other M3 partners will work together to deal with this challenge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The drug menace is not fully under control.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will fight with our heart and soul.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In English): Employment is another key in breaking the offending cycle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about support for ex-offenders to find jobs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Ex-offenders who are unable to secure jobs on their own, can apply for jobs via SCORE's online job portal or contact SCORE's Employment Assistance Unit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about steps taken to increase the employability of ex-offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: First, Prisons School has launched a Diploma programme in Business Practice (International Supply Chain Management) with Ngee Ann Polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Inmates can benefit from the projected increase in manpower demand of the logistics sector upon their release.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Second, since June 2018, SCORE has enhanced the Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) training in culinary skills to include advanced modules.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I visited Prisons last month and observed inmates learning to make chicken soup, not from ready-made sachets, but from scratch.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: With this certification, they can work at kitchens as kitchen helpers and progress the ranks to commissioned cooks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Third, SCORE has partnered Workforce Singapore (WSG) to emplace ex-offenders on short-term work stints under the Career Trial Programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The trial allows a prospective employer to assess performance and job fit for up to 480 hours, before offering an ex-offender permanent employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: No manpower cost is incurred as the training allowance is paid by WSG.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Since its November 2018 launch, 24 employers offering more than 150 vacancies have come on board.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And besides offering such programmes which are geared mainly for inmates with longer sentence, we have also reviewed how we can help inmates with short sentences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Last year, the National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism, a committee co-led by MSF and MHA, was set up to oversee national efforts to prevent offending and re-offending and enhance rehabilitation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Committee assessed that there was scope to offer targeted support for higher-risk inmates with sentences of less than a year, as a good number of them may still have a high risk of re-offending.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: And since June 2018, Prisons have started to provide psychology-based correctional programmes to higher-risk inmates serving between six months and a year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This group of inmates will undergo an abridged pre-release programme and a Reintegration Needs Assessment before release.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Prisons will also work with the National Council of Social Service on a pilot to place 60 higher-risk inmates with short sentences on voluntary case management after their release, to assist with reintegration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Keeping Singapore safe and secure is our promise to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I will focus on three areas: road safety, fire safety and counterterrorism.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked how MHA will address the upward trend in irresponsible driving, such as drink-driving and redlight-running.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since 2014, the Traffic Police has been doing its utmost to encourage responsible driving, nudge motorists to drive safely in camera zones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It has publicised the locations of its cameras, installed signage and blinker lights, and painted the cameras in bright colours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We want to ensure that irresponsible drivers receive sentences commensurate with the harm that they cause and are kept off the roads for longer periods of time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked if MHA would consider putting in place a tiered drink-driving approach that takes into account the effect of alcohol on probationary or young drivers, as compared to other drivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our laws currently do not differentiate alcohol limits to different classes of drivers, because we cannot make an a priori claim on the effect of alcohol on persons based on factors like age and experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Furthermore, Traffic Police do not enforce drink-driving offences based solely on whether one has violated the alcohol limit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These criteria apply to all drivers, regardless of age or driving experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the end, we must recognise that the problem of dangerous driving cannot be curbed by regulations alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since the launch of the "Use Your Roadsense" campaign in 2015, Traffic Police and its partners have been actively promoting graciousness and responsibility amongst various groups of road users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Road safety is a shared responsibility, and we all need to play our part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now speak on fire safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Low Thia Khiang asked how we can improve fire safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Singapore has one of the lowest rates of fire fatalities in the world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is owed largely to our high fire safety standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many of our fire safety provisions are incorporated at the design stage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, every residential unit is designed as a fire compartment to prevent the spread of fires to adjacent units.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Fire escape routes are designed to have adequate ventilation, while infrastructures, like rising mains and hose reels, are built in to aid firefighting operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Low Thia Khiang said it was important that residents know what to do in the event of a fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Public education is, indeed, a key priority for us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF regularly conducts events, like Emergency Preparedness block parties, to teach residents emergency response skills, including how to extinguish small household fires and how to evacuate from a smoke-logged room.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF also works closely with senior activity centres to conduct regular fire safety awareness workshops for the elderly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang asked about whether residents in super high-rise public residential buildings can safely evacuate during a fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our evacuation strategy for ensuring the safety of residents in such buildings is multi-layered.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Next, we are building up a strong corps of community volunteers to help with evacuations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF works closely with the Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committees and the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT), to direct evacuation procedures in the event of a fire incident.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These teams comprise grassroots leaders and residents staying in the vicinity who are trained to assist in evacuation and crowd control in an emergency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF familiarises them with the fire safety facilities unique to super high-rise residential buildings to ensure that they are equipped to perform their roles effectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These volunteers are key partners to manage fire incidents in their initial stages, until Home Team officers arrive on the scene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On site, Home Team officers will go door-to-door and facilitate the evacuation of residents who have yet to leave their units and, if necessary, will use the fire lifts to evacuate those with mobility issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF also devotes specific resources to educate residents living in such buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, SCDF conducts door-to-door engagements and evacuation exercises for the residents of these buildings to ensure that they are familiar with evacuation procedures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF has also produced a poster and disseminated a poster to specifically educate residents in such buildings on what they should and should not do in the event of a fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Many of our fire safety provisions are incorporated at the design stage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, every residential unit is designed as a fire compartment to prevent the spread of fires to adjacent units.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Fire escape routes are designed to have adequate ventilation, while infrastructures like rising mains and hosereels are built in to aid firefighting operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF regularly conducts events, like Emergency Preparedness block parties, to teach residents emergency response skills, such as how to put out small fires at home, or how to escape from a smoke-filled rooms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For super high-rise buildings, we require them to incorporate various fire safety measures in their design, such as refuge floors and fire lifts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also building up a strong corps of community volunteers to help with evacuations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF works closely with the C2E committees and CERT to direct evacuation procedures in the event of a fire incident.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These teams comprise grassroots leaders and residents staying in the vicinity who are trained to assist in evacuation and crowd control in an emergency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These volunteers are key partners to manage fire incidents in their initial stages, until Home Team officers arrive on the scene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On-site Home Team officers will go door-to-door and facilitate the evacuation of residents who have yet to leave their units and, if necessary, will use the fire lifts to evacuate those with mobility issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Jessica Tan also asked how we can improve fire safety standards for older buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, SCDF reviews the Fire Code constantly to stipulate new fire safety provisions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, a new requirement last year was for home fire alarm devices to be installed in all new residential premises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, changes to the Fire Code only apply to new buildings and buildings that undergo addition and alteration works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, it is an offence for certain parties, such as building owners, occupiers and industry professionals, to install non-compliant fire safety products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, it is not an offence if parties are involved in the supply of non-compliant fire safety products but stop short of installing them on buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With the amendments, SCDF will be able to take action against any errant party who use, or cause the use of, non-compliant fire safety products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SCDF will also be able to order errant parties to take remedial actions, such as recalling or stopping the sale of non-compliant products, and removing them from buildings if they have been installed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now speak on our counterterrorism efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The terrorism threat to Singapore remains high and we remain an attractive target to ISIS and other groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We may not have yet been hit but we certainly have been targeted and we must not take our security for granted.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about measures that MHA is taking to detect and deter self-radicalisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a stark increase from the 11 such cases that were detected between 2007 and 2014.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While the overall responsibility for counterterrorism lies with the Home Team, the community also plays an indispensable role, especially in detecting suspected cases of self-radicalisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families, friends and colleagues are best placed to notice such signs in an individual.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, Mr Mohamad Faishal bin Mohamad Razali who was detained under the ISA in April 2018, had told two of his friends about his plan to participate in armed violence overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: His friends and family members had tried to dissuade him but to no avail.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Eventually, someone who knew of his plans, alerted the authorities so that he could be prevented from continuing down the path of radicalisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, I encourage the public to report suspected cases as soon as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Early reporting not only prevents the commission of violence and loss of lives; it also gives the individual the best possible chance of being rehabilitated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our religious communities also played a critical role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, the Religious Rehabilitation Group is a voluntary group of Islamic scholars and teachers, who not only conduct counselling and rehabilitation for radicalised individuals, but also invest significant educational efforts to ward off extremist thinking in the general Islamic community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We cannot allow extremist ideologies to take root in our society, and we must safeguard our way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked for an update on SGSecure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SGSecure movement began by sensitising the public to the terror threat, and imparting basic information and skills to cope with an attack.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As awareness grew, we focused more on raising preparedness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have worked with workplaces, schools, neighbourhoods and places of worship to help them be crisis-ready.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the coming months, a new series of SGSecure initiatives will be rolled out.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They include holding SGSecure events at condominiums, more public roadshows, forming an SGSecure Responders Network to mobilise first responders from the community, and bringing together stakeholders from different domains to be part of the Community Response Round Table.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With these new initiatives, we hope to make participation in SGSecure programmes more accessible and to strengthen our whole-of-society response to the terror threat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: LastIy, I would like to address Mr Faisal Manap's question about the Police's standard procedure in replying to appeals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the face of public safety risks and the heightened terror threat, it is more important than ever for Singaporeans to partner the Home Team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We succeed only when the community stands with us, shares our vision and partakes of the same effort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together, we will build a safe and secure Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary only mentioned about NMPs as well as NCMPs' appeal is being treated as kind of a personal appeal.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: What I mentioned is what about for the PAP Branch Chairman?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I mentioned earlier in my reply, the Police will consider all proper representations which include representations from elected Members of Parliament and from GRAs on behalf of their own constituents, and their grassroots leaders.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if you do, can you please first check the facts and see if the person was also a GRA, because Police are very clear, they will respond to Members of Parliament and they will respond to GRAs.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It does not matter if they have any other positions, but I think you should check and let us know whether that person is also a GRA, and I am sure he would have been.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: It was not mentioned that the appointment was a GRA.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police will respond, like other Government agencies, to Members of Parliament and GRAs, regardless of any other appointments they may hold.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Can I ask the Ministry with regard to my cut: what is the roadmap for Singaporeans with stepchildren in terms of their children getting their PR or citizenship if they cannot be legally adopted, as I have explained in my cut?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is primarily to safeguard the interest of the child and the public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is why we require the adoption, to formally establish the parent-child relationship between them in the eyes of the law.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The effect that this has is to put the legal status of the child beyond question.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For the child, it clearly establishes that his adoptive parents have legal responsibilities and obligations to care for him.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is also in our public interest as there is no ambiguity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because adoption is a serious matter, obviously, the process has to be rigorous and effort must be made to ensure that the child's welfare is safeguarded.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Through the investigations, some prospective adopters may be assessed to be unsuitable and these adoptions cannot proceed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Others may not be able to adopt their stepchild if the natural parent does not agree to the adoption.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And in these circumstances, the law already allows the Family Justice Courts to dispense with the requirement if it is the Court's judgment that adequate effort has been made and there is no reason to believe that the natural parent is contesting for the custody of the child.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If the Court is satisfied after it has assessed, it can decide to dispense with the requirement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If I may summarise, the process is there for good reasons and, instead of doing away with the process, I think let us instead help the deserving families to meet the requirements and to allow the Court to exercise its judgment.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can I ask the Minister, currently, is it an offence for someone who knows of a friend or a family member who is thinking of committing a terrorist act or after he has been self-radicalised, and not to report?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It depends much on what is it that the person is planning to do and the degree of association, the help or other kinds of assistance the person who knows has given.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And quite a number of the arrests that the Internal Security Department has made over the years have, in fact, been based on reports from family members, friends, others who have noticed that something is not quite right.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Faisal, if it is a new question, I would allow it.

speaker: The Chairman
text: But if it is a question which has already been answered, I will disallow it.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Just now, it was mentioned that apart from the elected Members of Parliament as well as GRAs making appeal, any other appeals will be taken as a personal appeal.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, am I right to say that appeals of NCMPs, NMPs and a political party Branch Chairman will also be considered as normal appeal, and there is no merit to it?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Is there no further consideration or special consideration being made or being looked into when these appeals come from these groups of people, as I mentioned just now?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Faisal, that question has already been answered, but I will allow Mr Shanmugam to repeat the answer again.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One is: as a Government, we try and say "no wrong door".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, if a person is entitled to make an appeal on behalf of somebody, for example, a GRA, then if it comes from some other letterhead or he does not mention that designation, nevertheless the agencies will check.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If he is a GRA, then it is a little bit pointless to write back to him and say – and meanwhile, time is taken up – "Send it to us on a different note, mention your designation and then we will deal with it".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think that is a very bureaucratic way of dealing with it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Because the interest of the Government is also to deal with the appeal in the interest of the residents.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At the same time, there have to be some rules of who the agencies will respond to and will not respond to.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They cannot respond to everybody who purports to write on behalf of somebody else.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How do we know if, indeed, that it is so?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If it is a GRA or a Member of Parliament, then we can hold that person responsible for whatever is said.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And as Mr Faisal Manap knows, some of these representations can have legal consequences as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And as Mr Faisal Manap will know, sometimes, there is a grey area.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Often, that is what the person who is writing the appeal letter is trying to do.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When the Police respond, whether it is yes or no, and where necessary, the reasons are set out, so that anyone can look at this and ask further questions.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The Minister mentioned about the Singaporean identity and to have our own Singapore identity.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And the second thing I would like to ask is, especially our Muslim youths, who are easily influenced by external influences, extremist thinking, very black-and-white sort of preachings from outside Singapore, would it be of interest to reform the Singapore Muslim identity campaign that was launched sometime ago by Dr Yaacob Ibrahim?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Would it be of interest to bring it back again, to sort of protect our youths and to educate them, to inoculate them against these influences from outside?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think the primary essence of the Member's question is on how we deal with the ongoing programme on Singapore Muslim Identity.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It really needs to be answered by the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If I can take one step back, the point the Member made about young Muslims finding it very appealing to look at black-and-white preachings, I do not think that it is restricted to young Muslim youths.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think it cuts across many different religions, races.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Beyond religion, as you can see from different parts of the world, black-and-white soundbytes are appealing, even in very mature democracies.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is much easier to listen to simple soundbytes rather than a more reasoned point of thinking.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It does take time to put it across.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But we know what the challenges are in terms of the trends that have come across.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We need to try and bring them together and ensure that the secular space that we have created for politics is there.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And at the same time, one pursues freedom to practice one's religion, and we guarantee that; at the same time, to create and make sure that the common space we have created is maintained, all will have to contribute to that – the different religious organisations, faiths, people, secular organisations, the Government.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If there are no further clarifications, Mr Christopher de Souza, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It was an extremely busy 2018 for MHA.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And 2019 and 2020 look to be full ones, too.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We would also like to thank the Home Team, including the SPF, SCDF, Police Coast Guard, Prisons, ICA for keeping Singapore safe.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We sometimes take it for granted, but every now and then, it is nice to say a big thank you to the Home Team.
